posts.cooked:
I was reading the background of the 'Vengence' Baron Blade and something caught my eye...

"... his most dasterdly invention: the regression seurm... He went through a hundred test subjects with a 0% survival rate. Baron Blade was getting desperate until he recieved reports from one of his testing facilities that one plucky test subject had not only survived, but had actually devolped rudimentary physical powers as a result! This was a great breakthrough but, came with a notable setback. The subject had escaped the testing facility.

After a frustering lack of luck in reapproating the subject..."

 

This got me thinking about Rook City, specifically Spite. (snipit plagurized from the book below)

"... He was offered a deal: volunteer as test specimen for a secret project by Pike Industeries and have his sentence commuted to life imprisonment. Donovan and a number of other prisoners were subjected to a series of experimental drugs and mutagens, which killed most of the subjects in the first test. Donovan not only survived the tests, he flourished, granting him terrible strength and power by the chemicals in his system. He escaped the lab, but was overwhelmed with hunger and need. As Spite, he continues killing more and more victims and breaking into Pike Labratories to ingest coruptive substances."

and from the website

"Offical Note: With the destruction of the Barzakh wing, please destory this testing log and all other testing logs from that wing. Also, report all subjects from R.C. Penitentary as 'lost, unrecoverable' and stop any additional transfers."

 

My questions: Did The Chairman create Spite with the help of Baron Blade? Did Baron Blade actually create Spite, using Pike Labs? Is there another Spite running around the Multiverse?

 

 

Anyone else have theories? Let's hear 'em.

posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
Conspiracy theories are a thing I have plenty of!  Here are a bunch of them.

1. The Chairman is behind all the major events of the multiverse. I think that Pike is the driving force for the overarching plotline.  I think that he bankrolls the baron (as a distraction and a source of tech), provides chemicals, weapons, etc to pretty much everyone, and is constantly searching for new avenues for personal power. The guy is immortal (for a given value thereof), and I'm thinking that he's willing to destroy anyone and everyone else in his quest.  I wouldn't be surprised if he pops up again as the final bad guy, having attained cosmic-level power.  If there is ANYONE willing to sell out the earth, turn it into grey goo, or upload his brain, its going to be Pike.

2. Mr Fixer is blind.  None of his cards depict his eyes (they are either covered by the hat, or in shadow), and his new costume has no eye holes. this also explains why the Chairman revealed himself to Fixer in "Undivided Attention".  He knew that even if Fixer survived, he would not be able to provide a physical description 

3. Mr Fixer was killed (for a  given value thereof) by the operative.  He was kept barely alive by the Chairman as a bargaining chip, should other heroes come calling.  He spent a lot of time in that place between life and death. 

4. The other members of Dark Watch were the ones that took down the Operative (probably assisted by Parse, given the arrows sticking out of the Operative).  Pike made a deal to escape by giving them back Mr. Fixer.  This could possibly explain why Mr. Fixer looks younger, and the "bitter" part of Bitter Strike.  

5. It is also possible that DW Fixer is a clone, grown in the biomimetic plasma vat. This could satisfy the statement that "if we ever see him without his hat, he's dead.

6. The Operative is Brave Thiago's mother. 

7. Thiago is going to become Legacy (in name, if not power) when Pauline decides not to continue the Legacy name.  It is entirely possible that Paul Parsons will also take on a new name, thus satisfying the statement that "there is only one Legacy"

8. Chrono-ranger is stuck in a time loop where he becomes plague rat.  I know that there are a bunch of reasons that this doesn't work, but I like this too much to give it up!

9. Expatriette and Setback are an item as of Dark Watch.

9. Expatriette is developing powers, and her story is a 3-parter.

The first part is her with no powers, being driven away and experiencing prejudice.  We see her getting a thrill from taking down super-powered people because of how they treated her.  

The second part is the Dark Watch Expat.  She's started to think that she has some sort of powers, but doesn't know their full extent.  she certainly seems ridiculously hard to kill, and might even be coming back from the dead.  she starts to re-evaluate the thrill she gets from taking down super-powered people (since she knows many good ones, and might be one herself).  She becomes more thoughtful and hangs back to prepare instead of charging ins guns blazing (the shift from playing an extra card to aiming and sniper rifles).  She also starts a relationship with Setback, and sees someone who (like herself) obviously has SOME sort of power.  They help each other, and compliment each other's weaknesses. 

The third part is yet to come.  I think that Expat needs to confront Dawn on even terms, in the full bloom of her power.  It seems like an important plot point for Dawn to see that she COULD have had the daughter that she always wanted (in terms of power), but drove her away with thesame kind of prejudices that Dawn experienced in her own childhood.

 

At least thats what I think.

I am firmly in the camp that the Dragon/Chinese Master is behind Fixer's resurection. The Why/How of that is impossible to say, but the circumstansial evidence is pretty compelling (and even more compelling still if you want to include vengeance stuff, but not nessesary I dont think).

  4. The Dark Watch seem to have a more supernatural focus. I imagined the Operative was dispatched well before the Dark Watch was ever founded. With all the arrows in her back, though, Parse might have killed her. Though that feels like it would be extreamly out of place for Parse. But we know next to nothign about her morals. Not too many characters use arrows either. I assume Chrono's Composite Bow doesnt shoot arrows right? Right??

  5. Could be a clone. Could also be just sorta undead? If Spite is the walking dead, maybe Fixer exists in the same fashion.

  6. Certainly possible!

  7. He won't become Legacy. He is not of the bloodline, so he would never be a true Legacy. His shirt having Legacy's symbol isnt what is important with Thiago. It's the drive/need/desire to BE a superhero that is whats important to take away. Thiago 100% has a larger role to play, and I fully expect him to become a real hero at some point. It wont be under the Legacy name though.

  9. This is very compelling. There is every reason in the world to think that Expat indeed has some sort of power, even if she doesnt know it.

posts.cooked:
Legacy is as much about standing up for what is right, being a leader, and a symbol for courage as having powers.  I think that Thiago has those qualities in spades.  If the Operative is his mother, its entirely possible that he'll have access to powers later on.  I'll stand by my theory.

 

the Operative and Mr. fixer  both have the same tattoo- the dragon.  The operative has it coiled around her arm in red, Fixer has it over his scar in blue. 

While this could signify some sort of dragon-inspired resurrection, there are other possibilities. 

 

1. It signifies that both of them have fought the dragon (literally), and gained power in the process.

We've seen that Fixer has a card depicting a fight against the dragon.  Perhaps fighting it gave him strength/vigor/life?

 

2. It signifies that both of them have fought the dragon (metaphorically), and are part of a secret society.

It could be that once you've attained a certain mastery of the martial arts, you have to face your fears and figure out what is most important to you.  this fight can take many forms.

 

For the operative, it was a literal fight (in that she prizes strength above all), and so when she emerged triumphant (this could easily be the fight depicted on her character card, or her surviving the fight depicted on her incap), she gained physical power and a tattoo on the arm (to signify outer strength).

For Mr fixer, it was an internal fight, in that his greatest failure was walking away from the Operative when she was a child and giving up for many years. (signified in that the fight against the dragon takes place in a featureless void).  It was a fight between letting go and dying, or accepting that there was much left to do and he couldn't walk away again.  In winning, he gained a measure of his lost youth back, and a tattoo of the dragon over his scar (to remind him of his greatest failure).

the Operative and Mr. fixer  both have the same tattoo- the dragon.  The operative has it coiled around her arm in red, Fixer has it over his scar in blue. 

While this could signify some sort of dragon-inspired resurrection, there are other possibilities. 

 

1. It signifies that both of them have fought the dragon (literally), and gained power in the process.

We've seen that Fixer has a card depicting a fight against the dragon.  Perhaps fighting it gave him strength/vigor/life?

 

2. It signifies that both of them have fought the dragon (metaphorically), and are part of a secret society.

It could be that once you've attained a certain mastery of the martial arts, you have to face your fears and figure out what is most important to you.  this fight can take many forms.

 

For the operative, it was a literal fight (in that she prizes strength above all), and so when she emerged triumphant (this could easily be the fight depicted on her character card, or her surviving the fight depicted on her incap), she gained physical power and a tattoo on the arm (to signify outer strength).

For Mr fixer, it was an internal fight, in that his greatest failure was walking away from the Operative when she was a child and giving up for many years. (signified in that the fight against the dragon takes place in a featureless void).  It was a fight between letting go and dying, or accepting that there was much left to do and he couldn't walk away again.  In winning, he gained a measure of his lost youth back, and a tattoo of the dragon over his scar (to remind him of his greatest failure).

Legacy is as much about standing up for what is right, being a leader, and a symbol for courage as having powers.  

To people, sure. But Legacy wasn't simply chosen by the first Legacy. It was picked because of the enscription on the ring "Furthering your father's legacy". The name Legacy is passed down, much like the Legacy ring, as a way to carry on their ancestor's truimphs. I can't see them passing down a family heierloom, just because they encountered someone who tarnished the name in another timeline.

There is also the fact that on Sentinel Tactics, Legacy is still seen wearing the Lantern and the Legacy ring. He's still very much Legacy.

posts.cooked:
I'm very much with you on the metaphoric side of the tattoo.

A few things. The Operative, more than likely, has the tattoo before the events of her incapp side (whatever that may entail).

The dragon tattoo absolutly signals a significant connection between Fixer, Opperative, and his "resurection". It also probably speaks to the deeper nemesis connection between Fixer and the Chairman/Opperative, which currently is pretty paper thin. 

I really want to connect this Chinese Master/Dragon dude with the Chinese Master mentioned in Nightmists bio. You know, the one that taught her all about the mists, her curse, and her power. 

 

At some point, the Operative might have trained under this Master. He could have his own dojo (similar to Fixer's in a way) where he trains assasins and all that good stuff. I'm having imagry of a Kill Bill Vol.1 kinda deal with the crazy 88. Lots of fighters. The Operative might very well be a disiple of this Master (in addition to her day job of running security for the Chairman). How the Operative dies and the reasons for why the Master would want to bring back Fixer is a total mystery. Keep in mind, this Master and Fixer do not look like friends. They fought before the resurection.

After Fixer dies (by the Operatives hand), Fixer might very well have found peace in the afterlife. Meditation, I think, hints at this. I believe the art for that card is intentially hyper-stylized (more so than normal) to represent that enlightened state. Taking Fixer out of this inner peace of the afterlife could very well have sinister intentions, especially if the dude/dragon has particular reach into the underworld (my current speculation says he does). And he probably brings Fixer back just in time to see his own friends and allies kill the Operative. His old student. Someone who Fixer had let down and now there is no fix for this. That could turn even the most stout of heros bitter.
